title.value: Contrast-agnostic deep learning–based registration pipeline: Validation in spinal cord multimodal MRI data
title.justification: The title clearly communicates the focus of the paper, which is about a deep learning-based registration pipeline specifically validated on spinal cord multimodal MRI data.
title.quote: Contrast-agnostic deep learning–based registration pipeline: Validation in spinal cord multimodal MRI data

extractions.description: The paper introduces a deep learning-based registration pipeline, enhancing SynthMorph, for medical image registration. It is validated using spinal cord multimodal MRI data to address challenges related to anatomical variations. The pipeline features cascaded models for handling large and fine deformations and has been tested against benchmarks in terms of registration accuracy and computational speed.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is fundamentally concerned with medical image registration in MRI data, aiming to improve registration accuracy and speed. It does not address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development directly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This proposed pipeline provides an easy-to-use, accurate and fast solution for multimodal 3D registration. The code and trained models are freely available at https://github.com/ivadomed/multimodal-registration.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of this paper is the enhancement and validation of a medical image registration pipeline within the field of MRI, which doesn't pertain to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: This work extends the original SynthMorph approach by implementing a registration method consisting of two cascaded models to accommodate images with large displacements.

secondary_categories.justification: While the paper discusses innovations in medical imaging technology, it does not relate secondary themes to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: Another possibility is to overcome ground truth deformations during the learning process by using unsupervised deep-learning methods, which have been increasingly developed in recent years for registration (6).

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no alignment with the provided Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories, as the focus is purely medical and not aligned with environmental themes.
primary_sub_category.quote: The difficulty with unsupervised learning lies in defining an appropriate loss function without using ground truth deformations.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The secondary aspects of this research do not overlap with the listed Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The drawback of traditional methods is that they often require substantial computational time, up to tens of minutes to even hours on a CPU (3) for deformable registration of large 3D MRI data.

applications.justification: The primary application of this research is to provide a faster and more accurate registration model for multimodal MRI data focusing on the spinal cord.
applications.quote: The developed registration pipeline provides an easy-to-use, accurate and fast solution for multimodal 3D registration.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not propose any new category relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Results demonstrate better registration accuracy compared with the benchmark and about 24–30 times faster on CPUs depending on the image size.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new sub-category as the paper’s focus is not within the remit of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a comprehensive framework for 3D MRI image registration based on deep-learning models trained with the SynthMorph strategy.
